subject: [PATCH v8 00/30] mm: PMD-level swap entries for anonymous THPs

reviews.author: Usama Arif (author)
reviews.summary: The author addressed a concern about the naming of the function pmd_to_softleaf_folio() in leafops.h, explaining that it actually decodes the softleaf entry and returns the referenced folio, not converts a PMD to a folio. The author confirmed no functional change was intended.
reviews.raw_body:
pmd_to_softleaf_folio() reads as if it converted a PMD into a folio. What
it does is decode the softleaf entry stored in the PMD and return the
folio that entry references - the direction softleaf_to_folio() already
spells out.

No functional change intended.

Suggested-by: Dev Jain <dev.jain@arm.com>
Signed-off-by: Usama Arif <usama.arif@linux.dev>
Acked-by: David Hildenbrand (Arm) <david@kernel.org>
Reviewed-by: Lorenzo Stoakes (ARM) <ljs@kernel.org>
Reviewed-by: Zi Yan <ziy@nvidia.com>
Acked-by: Kiryl Shutsemau (Meta) <kas@kernel.org>
Reviewed-by: Barry Song <baohua@kernel.org>
Reviewed-by: Baoquan He <baoquan.he@linux.dev>
Reviewed-by: Qi Zheng <qi.zheng@linux.dev>
---
 include/linux/leafops.h | 4 ++--
 mm/huge_memory.c        | 2 +-
 2 files changed, 3 insertions(+), 3 deletions(-)

diff --git a/include/linux/leafops.h b/include/linux/leafops.h
index 4c1476ae32343..7c13c58a5e218 100644
--- a/include/linux/leafops.h
+++ b/include/linux/leafops.h
@@ -657,7 +657,7 @@ static inline bool pmd_is_valid_softleaf(pmd_t pmd)
 }
 
 /**
- * pmd_to_softleaf_folio() - Convert the PMD entry to a folio.
+ * pmd_softleaf_to_folio() - Convert the PMD softleaf entry to a folio.
  * @pmd: PMD entry.
  *
  * The PMD entry is expected to be a valid PMD softleaf entry.
@@ -665,7 +665,7 @@ static inline bool pmd_is_valid_softleaf(pmd_t pmd)
  * Returns: the folio the softleaf entry references if this is a valid softleaf
  * entry, otherwise NULL.
  */
-static inline struct folio *pmd_to_softleaf_folio(pmd_t pmd)
+static inline struct folio *pmd_softleaf_to_folio(pmd_t pmd)
 {
 	const softleaf_t entry = softleaf_from_pmd(pmd);
 
diff --git a/mm/huge_memory.c b/mm/huge_memory.c
index 7140a1031fb2e..ee8d46827ffdc 100644
--- a/mm/huge_memory.c
+++ b/mm/huge_memory.c
@@ -2518,7 +2518,7 @@ static struct folio *normal_or_softleaf_folio_pmd(struct vm_area_struct *vma,
 
 	if (!thp_migration_supported())
 		WARN_ONCE(1, "Non present huge pmd without pmd migration enabled!");
-	return pmd_to_softleaf_folio(pmdval);
+	return pmd_softleaf_to_folio(pmdval);
 }
 
 static bool has_deposited_pgtable(struct vm_area_struct *vma, pmd_t pmdval,
--

reviews.author: Usama Arif (author)
reviews.summary: The author addressed a concern about how the PMD swap entry is handled on arm64, explaining that it's encoded exactly like a swap PTE and reusing existing helpers to wrap the PTE ones.
reviews.raw_body:
Prepare for keeping a PMD-mapped anonymous THP mapped by a PMD across the
swap round-trip, which makes PG_anon_exclusive have to survive in a swap
PMD and not just in a swap PTE.

arm64 encodes a swap PMD exactly like a swap PTE, so the new helpers wrap
the PTE ones and reuse PTE_SWP_EXCLUSIVE.

Cc: Catalin Marinas <catalin.marinas@arm.com>
Cc: Will Deacon <will@kernel.org>
Signed-off-by: Usama Arif <usama.arif@linux.dev>
---
 arch/arm64/include/asm/pgtable.h | 6 ++++++
 1 file changed, 6 insertions(+)

diff --git a/arch/arm64/include/asm/pgtable.h b/arch/arm64/include/asm/pgtable.h
index e89ec5f4787b4..d3f53a601aed3 100644
--- a/arch/arm64/include/asm/pgtable.h
+++ b/arch/arm64/include/asm/pgtable.h
@@ -599,6 +599,12 @@ static inline int pmd_protnone(pmd_t pmd)
 #define pmd_swp_clear_uffd(pmd) \
 				pte_pmd(pte_swp_clear_uffd(pmd_pte(pmd)))
 #endif /* CONFIG_HAVE_ARCH_USERFAULTFD_WP */
+#ifdef CONFIG_ARCH_HAS_PMD_SOFTLEAVES
+#define pmd_swp_exclusive(pmd)	pte_swp_exclusive(pmd_pte(pmd))
+#define pmd_swp_mkexclusive(pmd)	pte_pmd(pte_swp_mkexclusive(pmd_pte(pmd)))
+#define pmd_swp_clear_exclusive(pmd) \
+				pte_pmd(pte_swp_clear_exclusive(pmd_pte(pmd)))
+#endif
 
 #define pmd_write(pmd)		pte_write(pmd_pte(pmd))
 
--

reviews.author: Usama Arif (author)
reviews.summary: The author is addressing a concern about how to handle PG_anon_exclusive in the context of PMD-mapped anonymous THPs being swapped out and back in, specifically for LoongArch architecture. The author explains that they are adding new helpers to handle this case by introducing a new bit _PAGE_SWP_EXCLUSIVE, which will be used to mark the PMD as exclusive during swap. This change is implemented in the arch/loongarch/include/asm/pgtable.h file.

reviews.author: Usama Arif (author)
reviews.summary: The author addressed a concern about the powerpc variant of PG_anon_exclusive needing to survive in a swap PMD, not just a swap PTE. They explained that book3s64 builds a swap PMD by running the PTE encoding over pmd_pte(), and added new macros for soft-dirty PMD helpers on powerpc.
reviews.raw_body:
Prepare for keeping a PMD-mapped anonymous THP mapped by a PMD across the
swap round-trip, which makes PG_anon_exclusive have to survive in a swap
PMD and not just in a swap PTE.

book3s64 builds a swap PMD by running the PTE encoding over pmd_pte(), so
the PMD helpers wrap the PTE ones and reuse _PAGE_SWP_EXCLUSIVE, exactly
as the soft-dirty PMD helpers next to them do. It is also the only powerpc
variant that selects ARCH_HAS_PMD_SOFTLEAVES, via PPC_THP.

Cc: Madhavan Srinivasan <maddy@linux.ibm.com>
Signed-off-by: Usama Arif <usama.arif@linux.dev>
---
 arch/powerpc/include/asm/book3s/64/pgtable.h | 6 ++++++
 1 file changed, 6 insertions(+)

diff --git a/arch/powerpc/include/asm/book3s/64/pgtable.h b/arch/powerpc/include/asm/book3s/64/pgtable.h
index dff8790a047db..458c85cebfa65 100644
--- a/arch/powerpc/include/asm/book3s/64/pgtable.h
+++ b/arch/powerpc/include/asm/book3s/64/pgtable.h
@@ -1060,6 +1060,12 @@ static inline pte_t *pmdp_ptep(pmd_t *pmd)
 #endif
 #endif /* CONFIG_HAVE_ARCH_SOFT_DIRTY */
 
+#ifdef CONFIG_ARCH_HAS_PMD_SOFTLEAVES
+#define pmd_swp_mkexclusive(pmd)	pte_pmd(pte_swp_mkexclusive(pmd_pte(pmd)))
+#define pmd_swp_exclusive(pmd)		pte_swp_exclusive(pmd_pte(pmd))
+#define pmd_swp_clear_exclusive(pmd)	pte_pmd(pte_swp_clear_exclusive(pmd_pte(pmd)))
+#endif
+
 #ifdef CONFIG_ARCH_HAS_PTE_PROTNONE
 static inline int pmd_protnone(pmd_t pmd)
 {

reviews.summary: The author addressed a concern about how to handle PG_anon_exclusive in the context of PMD-mapped anonymous THPs being swapped out and back in, explaining that it needs to survive in a swap PMD and not just a PTE. The author provided new helpers for RISC-V that wrap the existing PTE ones and reuse _PAGE_SWP_EXCLUSIVE.
reviews.raw_body:
Prepare for keeping a PMD-mapped anonymous THP mapped by a PMD across the
swap round-trip, which makes PG_anon_exclusive have to survive in a swap
PMD and not just in a swap PTE.

riscv encodes a swap PMD exactly like a swap PTE, so the new helpers wrap
the PTE ones and reuse _PAGE_SWP_EXCLUSIVE.

Cc: Paul Walmsley <pjw@kernel.org>
Cc: Palmer Dabbelt <palmer@dabbelt.com>
Cc: Albert Ou <aou@eecs.berkeley.edu>
Signed-off-by: Usama Arif <usama.arif@linux.dev>
Reviewed-by: David Hildenbrand (Arm) <david@kernel.org>
---
 arch/riscv/include/asm/pgtable.h | 15 +++++++++++++++
 1 file changed, 15 insertions(+)

diff --git a/arch/riscv/include/asm/pgtable.h b/arch/riscv/include/asm/pgtable.h
index d48f90140841e..b644db16bda94 100644
--- a/arch/riscv/include/asm/pgtable.h
+++ b/arch/riscv/include/asm/pgtable.h
@@ -1219,6 +1219,21 @@ static inline pte_t pte_swp_clear_exclusive(pte_t pte)
 }
 
 #ifdef CONFIG_ARCH_HAS_PMD_SOFTLEAVES
+static inline bool pmd_swp_exclusive(pmd_t pmd)
+{
+	return pte_swp_exclusive(pmd_pte(pmd));
+}
+
+static inline pmd_t pmd_swp_mkexclusive(pmd_t pmd)
+{
+	return pte_pmd(pte_swp_mkexclusive(pmd_pte(pmd)));
+}
+
+static inline pmd_t pmd_swp_clear_exclusive(pmd_t pmd)
+{
+	return pte_pmd(pte_swp_clear_exclusive(pmd_pte(pmd)));
+}
+
 #define __pmd_to_swp_entry(pmd) ((swp_entry_t) { pmd_val(pmd) })
 #define __swp_entry_to_pmd(swp) __pmd((swp).val)
 #endif /* CONFIG_ARCH_HAS_PMD_SOFTLEAVES */

reviews.author: Usama Arif (author)
reviews.summary: The author addressed a concern about the handling of PMD-mapped anonymous THPs on s390 architecture, where swap PMDs are not just fake PTE swap entries but have their own layout (RSTE). To accommodate this, the author added an exclusive bit to the RSTE swap layout and modified the common code to handle it. The patch includes changes to arch/s390/include/asm/pgtable.h.
reviews.raw_body:
Prepare for keeping a PMD-mapped anonymous THP mapped by a PMD across the
swap round-trip, which makes PG_anon_exclusive have to survive in a swap
PMD and not just in a swap PTE.

s390 is the one architecture where a swap PMD is not a swap PTE in
disguise: it is an RSTE with its own layout, converted to a fake PTE swap
entry for the common code. Give it its own exclusive bit rather than
borrowing the PTE-format macro, and document it in the RSTE swap layout,
where bit 52 was listed as unused.

Cc: Alexander Gordeev <agordeev@linux.ibm.com>
Cc: Gerald Schaefer <gerald.schaefer@linux.ibm.com>
Cc: Heiko Carstens <hca@linux.ibm.com>
Cc: Vasily Gorbik <gor@linux.ibm.com>
Signed-off-by: Usama Arif <usama.arif@linux.dev>
---
 arch/s390/include/asm/pgtable.h | 20 ++++++++++++++++++--
 1 file changed, 18 insertions(+), 2 deletions(-)

diff --git a/arch/s390/include/asm/pgtable.h b/arch/s390/include/asm/pgtable.h
index 2d5c2ab06de98..afd886edf0594 100644
--- a/arch/s390/include/asm/pgtable.h
+++ b/arch/s390/include/asm/pgtable.h
@@ -333,6 +333,7 @@ void setup_protection_map(void);
 /* Common bits in region and segment table entries, for swap entries */
 #define _RST_ENTRY_COMM		0x0010	/* Common-Region/Segment, marks swap entry */
 #define _RST_ENTRY_INVALID	0x0020	/* invalid region/segment table entry */
+#define _RST_ENTRY_SWP_EXCLUSIVE 0x0800	/* SW exclusive swap bit, see mk_swap_rste() */
 
 #define _CRST_ENTRIES	2048	/* number of region/segment table entries */
 #define _PAGE_ENTRIES	256	/* number of page table entries	*/
@@ -893,6 +894,21 @@ static inline pmd_t pmd_clear_soft_dirty(pmd_t pmd)
 }
 
 #ifdef CONFIG_ARCH_HAS_PMD_SOFTLEAVES
+static inline pmd_t pmd_swp_mkexclusive(pmd_t pmd)
+{
+	return set_pmd_bit(pmd, __pgprot(_RST_ENTRY_SWP_EXCLUSIVE));
+}
+
+static inline bool pmd_swp_exclusive(pmd_t pmd)
+{
+	return pmd_val(pmd) & _RST_ENTRY_SWP_EXCLUSIVE;
+}
+
+static inline pmd_t pmd_swp_clear_exclusive(pmd_t pmd)
+{
+	return clear_pmd_bit(pmd, __pgprot(_RST_ENTRY_SWP_EXCLUSIVE));
+}
+
 #define pmd_swp_soft_dirty(pmd)		pmd_soft_dirty(pmd)
 #define pmd_swp_mksoft_dirty(pmd)	pmd_mksoft_dirty(pmd)
 #define pmd_swp_clear_soft_dirty(pmd)	pmd_clear_soft_dirty(pmd)
@@ -1900,15 +1916,15 @@ static inline swp_entry_t __swp_entry(unsigned long type, unsigned long offset)
  * Bits 59 and 63 are used to indicate the swap entry. Bit 58 marks the rste
  * as invalid.
  * A swap entry is indicated by bit pattern (rste & 0x011) == 0x010
- * |			  offset			|Xtype |11TT|S0|
+ * |			  offset			|Etype |11TT|S0|
  * |0000000000111111111122222222223333333333444444444455|555555|5566|66|
  * |0123456789012345678901234567890123456789012345678901|234567|8901|23|
  *
  * Bits 0-51 store the offset.
+ * Bit 52 (E) is used to remember PG_anon_exclusive (_RST_ENTRY_SWP_EXCLUSIVE).
  * Bits 53-57 store the type.
  * Bit 62 (S) is used for softdirty tracking.
  * Bits 60-61 (TT) indicate the table type: 0x01 for REGION3 and 0x00 for SEGMENT.
- * Bit 52 (X) is unused.
  */
 
 #define __SWP_OFFSET_MASK_RSTE	((1UL << 52) - 1)
--

reviews.author: Usama Arif (author)
reviews.summary: The author addresses a concern about the handling of PG_anon_exclusive in swap PMDs, explaining that x86-64 encodes swap PMDs like swap PTEs and reusing the _PAGE_SWP_EXCLUSIVE bit to preserve exclusivity. The author also adds new helpers for pmd_swp_mkexclusive and pmd_swp_clear_exclusive.
reviews.raw_body:
Prepare for keeping a PMD-mapped anonymous THP mapped by a PMD across the
swap round-trip, which makes PG_anon_exclusive have to survive in a swap
PMD and not just in a swap PTE.

x86-64 encodes a swap PMD exactly like a swap PTE, so the new helpers reuse
_PAGE_SWP_EXCLUSIVE, bit 3, which the swap-entry layout already reserves
for PG_anon_exclusive. 32-bit x86 aliases that bit to _PAGE_PSE and does
not select ARCH_HAS_PMD_SOFTLEAVES; assert that, because an exclusive swap
PMD would otherwise be pmd_present().

Cc: Thomas Gleixner <tglx@kernel.org>
Cc: Ingo Molnar <mingo@redhat.com>
Cc: Borislav Petkov <bp@alien8.de>
Cc: Dave Hansen <dave.hansen@linux.intel.com>
Cc: x86@kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Usama Arif <usama.arif@linux.dev>
Reviewed-by: Kiryl Shutsemau (Meta) <kas@kernel.org>
Reviewed-by: David Hildenbrand (Arm) <david@kernel.org>
---
 arch/x86/include/asm/pgtable.h | 20 ++++++++++++++++++++
 1 file changed, 20 insertions(+)

diff --git a/arch/x86/include/asm/pgtable.h b/arch/x86/include/asm/pgtable.h
index d551120a7c889..c35dfa6ceda05 100644
--- a/arch/x86/include/asm/pgtable.h
+++ b/arch/x86/include/asm/pgtable.h
@@ -1525,6 +1525,26 @@ static inline pte_t pte_swp_clear_exclusive(pte_t pte)
 	return pte_clear_flags(pte, _PAGE_SWP_EXCLUSIVE);
 }
 
+#ifdef CONFIG_ARCH_HAS_PMD_SOFTLEAVES
+/* 32-bit aliases this to _PAGE_PSE, making an exclusive swap PMD present. */
+static_assert(_PAGE_SWP_EXCLUSIVE != _PAGE_PSE);
+
+static inline pmd_t pmd_swp_mkexclusive(pmd_t pmd)
+{
+	return pmd_set_flags(pmd, _PAGE_SWP_EXCLUSIVE);
+}
+
+static inline bool pmd_swp_exclusive(pmd_t pmd)
+{
+	return pmd_flags(pmd) & _PAGE_SWP_EXCLUSIVE;
+}
+
+static inline pmd_t pmd_swp_clear_exclusive(pmd_t pmd)
+{
+	return pmd_clear_flags(pmd, _PAGE_SWP_EXCLUSIVE);
+}
+#endif
+
 #ifdef CONFIG_HAVE_ARCH_SOFT_DIRTY
 static inline pte_t pte_swp_mksoft_dirty(pte_t pte)
 {
--

reviews.author: Usama Arif (author)
reviews.summary: The author addressed a concern about PMD swap entries being valid softleaf entries, acknowledging they carry no PFN and can also have the swap-exclusive marker. The author added pmd_is_swap_entry() to check for swap entries and modified softleaf_from_pmd() to strip all overlays unconditionally.

reviews.author: Usama Arif (author)
reviews.summary: The author is addressing a concern about the potential for data corruption due to overlapping PMD exclusive bits and swap type or offset fields, which would only be caught at runtime. The author has added tests to mirror pte_swap_exclusive_tests() at the PMD level.

reviews.author: Huacai Chen
reviews.summary:
Reviewer noted that the patch does not handle the case where a PMD swap entry is split and some slots are still backed by zswap's per-page store, which can lead to incorrect behavior when trying to load the range page by page.

Reviewer Huacai Chen suggested reordering the pmd_swp_exclusive, pmd_swp_mkexclusive, and pmd_swp_clear_exclusive functions to match the natural order of operations, citing that the RISC-V version already follows this order
reviews.raw_body:
Hi, Usama,

On Fri, Oct 2, 2026 at 5:55 PM Usama Arif <usama.arif@linux.dev> wrote:

---

I think the order should be pmd_swp_exclusive, pmd_swp_mkexclusive and
pmd_swp_clear_exclusive. That looks more natural.

The riscv version is already like this, but others are not.


Huacai

2026-10-02.patch_summary: This patch series introduces PMD-level swap entries for anonymous THPs, allowing huge mappings to survive the swap round-trip and reducing page-table overhead. When a PMD-mapped anonymous THP is swapped out, it is split into PTE-level swap entries. The new PMD swap entry is a compact page-table encoding that can be restored directly on swap-in without waiting for khugepaged to collapse the range later. This approach reduces major faults and swap I/O rate, resulting in improved performance. The patch series is ordered so that every consumer can handle PMD swap entries before the swap-out producer starts installing them.
